title: Joshua Chapter 8 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Joshua chapter 8 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Joshua Chapter 8 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Joshua Chapter 8.

questions.question: What did the LORD tell Joshua not to be when he was commanded to go up to Ai?
options: Fearful and dismayed
Fear not and be not dismayed
Proud and boastful
Hasty and reckless
questions.correctAnswer: Fear not and be not dismayed
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:1 states that the LORD said unto Joshua, 'Fear not, neither be thou dismayed'.

questions.question: According to the LORD's command in Joshua 8, what was Joshua to do with the spoil and cattle of Ai?
options: Destroy them
Take them for a prey unto yourselves
Give them to the Levites
Leave them untouched
questions.correctAnswer: Take them for a prey unto yourselves
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:2 commands that only the spoil and cattle of Ai shall be taken for a prey unto yourselves.

questions.question: How many mighty men of valour did Joshua choose to go up against Ai?
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:3 says Joshua chose out thirty thousand mighty men of valour.

questions.question: Where did Joshua command the men to lie in wait against the city of Ai?
options: In front of the city
Behind the city
On the east side of the city
Far away from the city
questions.correctAnswer: Behind the city
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:4 records Joshua commanding them to lie in wait against the city, even behind the city.

questions.question: What was Joshua and his people’s strategy when the men of Ai came out against them?
options: To stand their ground
To flee before them
To attack immediately
To negotiate peace
questions.correctAnswer: To flee before them
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:5 explains that Joshua and all the people would flee before them to draw them out from the city.

questions.question: Why did Joshua plan to flee before the men of Ai as they came out to fight?
options: Because they were afraid
To draw them out of the city
To surrender
To regroup with reinforcements
questions.correctAnswer: To draw them out of the city
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:6 states the men of Ai would pursue because they would think Israel was fleeing, thus drawing them out of the city.

questions.question: What did Joshua say the men lying in ambush should do after the men of Ai were drawn out?
options: Retreat quietly
Rise up and seize the city
Attack the pursuers
Set a trap outside the city
questions.correctAnswer: Rise up and seize the city
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:7 commands the men in ambush to rise up and seize upon the city.

questions.question: What were the men instructed to do with the city once they had taken it?
options: Make a peace treaty
Set the city on fire
Occupy the city peacefully
Leave the city intact
questions.correctAnswer: Set the city on fire
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:8 states they were to set the city on fire according to the LORD's commandment.

questions.question: Where did the men sent to lie in ambush dwell the night before the attack?
options: Between Bethel and Ai on the west side of Ai
Inside the city of Ai
On the north side of Ai
In the wilderness far from Ai
questions.correctAnswer: Between Bethel and Ai on the west side of Ai
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:9 tells that the men in ambush abode between Bethel and Ai on the west side of Ai.

questions.question: What did Joshua do early in the morning before going up to Ai?
options: He prayed alone
He sent spies into Ai
He numbered the people and went up with the elders
He built an altar
questions.correctAnswer: He numbered the people and went up with the elders
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:10 reports Joshua rose early, numbered the people, and went up with the elders before the people to Ai.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua and all the people of war pitched their camp on the south side of Ai.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:11 says they pitched on the north side of Ai, not the south.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua took about five thousand men to lie in ambush on the west side of the city.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:12 states Joshua took about five thousand men to lie in ambush between Bethel and Ai on the west side.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua commanded the men to go very far from the city while lying in wait.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:4 says 'go not very far from the city', so the command was to stay near.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD promised to deliver the city of Ai into the hand of Joshua and his men.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:7 states that the LORD your God will deliver the city into your hand.

questions.question: In Joshua 8, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Set the city on fire after capture
Lay an ambush behind the city
Choose thirty thousand mighty men to send away by night
Number the people early in the morning
questions.correctAnswer: Lay an ambush behind the city
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:2 commands to lay an ambush for the city behind it before choosing men or numbering the people.

medium.title: Joshua Chapter 8 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Joshua Chapter 8 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What strategy did Joshua and Israel use to defeat the men of Ai according to Joshua 8:13-16?
options: They attacked Ai directly with all their forces at once
They used a feigned retreat to lure the men of Ai out of the city
They negotiated a peace treaty before attacking
They waited for Ai to attack them inside the city
questions.correctAnswer: They used a feigned retreat to lure the men of Ai out of the city
questions.explanation: Joshua set an ambush and then pretended to flee, causing the men of Ai to pursue them and leave the city unguarded (Joshua 8:13-16).

questions.question: According to Joshua 8:17, what was the state of the city of Ai when its men went out to pursue Israel?
options: The city was heavily fortified and guarded
The city was left open and unprotected
The city was partially guarded by a few men
The gates were sealed shut
questions.correctAnswer: The city was left open and unprotected
questions.explanation: All the men of Ai and Bethel went out to pursue Israel, leaving the city open without anyone to guard it (Joshua 8:17).

questions.question: What command did the LORD give Joshua regarding the spear in his hand in Joshua 8:18?
options: Throw the spear into the city
Stretch out the spear toward Ai
Hide the spear until the battle ends
Break the spear as a sign of surrender
questions.correctAnswer: Stretch out the spear toward Ai
questions.explanation: The LORD instructed Joshua to stretch out the spear in his hand toward Ai as a sign that He would give the city into Joshua's hand (Joshua 8:18).

questions.question: What happened immediately after Joshua stretched out his spear toward the city according to Joshua 8:19?
options: The ambush rose quickly and took the city by storm
The men of Ai surrendered without a fight
The ambush was discovered and defeated
Joshua's men retreated back into the valley
questions.correctAnswer: The ambush rose quickly and took the city by storm
questions.explanation: As soon as Joshua stretched out his hand, the ambush arose quickly, entered the city, took it, and set it on fire (Joshua 8:19).

questions.question: How does Joshua 8:20 describe the reaction of the men of Ai when they saw the smoke of their burning city?
options: They fled in all directions and escaped
They were trapped and had no power to flee
They called for reinforcements from Bethel
They fought fiercely to reclaim the city
questions.correctAnswer: They were trapped and had no power to flee
questions.explanation: Seeing the smoke of the city, the men of Ai could not flee this way or that, and those who fled to the wilderness turned back upon their pursuers (Joshua 8:20).

questions.question: What does Joshua 8:21 teach about the relationship between faith in God's promise and obedience in battle?
options: Faith in God's promise leads to victory when obeying His commands
Obedience is unnecessary if one has enough soldiers
Victory depends only on the number of weapons used
Faith is irrelevant without good military strategy
questions.correctAnswer: Faith in God's promise leads to victory when obeying His commands
questions.explanation: When Joshua and Israel saw the smoke, confirming the ambush's success, they turned and struck down the men of Ai, showing that trusting God's promise and obeying His plan led to victory (Joshua 8:21).

questions.question: True or False: According to Joshua 8:22, none of the men of Ai escaped after Israel's attack.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verse states that Israel smote the men of Ai so that none escaped or remained alive (Joshua 8:22).

questions.question: In Joshua 8:23, what was done with the king of Ai following the battle?
options: He was killed in battle
He was taken alive and brought to Joshua
He escaped into the wilderness
He was made ruler under Joshua's authority
questions.correctAnswer: He was taken alive and brought to Joshua
questions.explanation: The king of Ai was captured alive and brought before Joshua (Joshua 8:23).

questions.question: How does Joshua 8:24 illustrate the thoroughness of Israel's obedience to God's command during the conquest of Ai?
options: Israel spared many of Ai's inhabitants
Israel only chased the enemy into the city
Israel pursued and completely destroyed all inhabitants in the field and wilderness
Israel negotiated peace after defeating Ai
questions.correctAnswer: Israel pursued and completely destroyed all inhabitants in the field and wilderness
questions.explanation: The Israelites did not cease until all inhabitants were consumed by the sword in the field and wilderness and then returned to destroy the city itself (Joshua 8:24).

questions.question: According to Joshua 8:25, approximately how many men of Ai fell on that day?
questions.explanation: The verse records that twelve thousand men of Ai fell that day (Joshua 8:25).

questions.question: What does Joshua 8:26 convey about Joshua's commitment to God's instructions during the battle?
options: He hesitated before completing the battle
He partially obeyed God's commands
He did not withdraw his hand until he utterly destroyed all inhabitants
He left some inhabitants alive to serve as slaves
questions.correctAnswer: He did not withdraw his hand until he utterly destroyed all inhabitants
questions.explanation: Joshua kept his hand stretched out with the spear until all inhabitants were completely destroyed, showing total obedience (Joshua 8:26).

questions.question: True or False: According to Joshua 8:27, Israel took the spoil and cattle of Ai as their own prey, in obedience to the LORD's command.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verse states that only the cattle and spoil were taken as prey according to the LORD's command (Joshua 8:27).

questions.question: What was done to the city of Ai after its capture according to Joshua 8:28?
options: It was rebuilt as a stronghold
It was made a permanent dwelling place for Israelites
It was burnt and made a heap of ruins forever
It was given to the priests as a holy city
questions.correctAnswer: It was burnt and made a heap of ruins forever
questions.explanation: Joshua burned the city and made it a desolation and heap forever (Joshua 8:28).

questions.question: What lesson about justice and honor can be learned from Joshua 8:29 regarding the treatment of the king of Ai?
options: The king was honored as a prisoner of war
The king was hanged and then his body was discarded publicly
The king was released after paying a ransom
The king was spared and made a servant
questions.correctAnswer: The king was hanged and then his body was discarded publicly
questions.explanation: The king of Ai was hanged until evening, then his body was taken down and cast at the city gate with a heap of stones raised over it (Joshua 8:29).

questions.question: What does Joshua 8:30-31 teach about the importance of worship and obedience after victory?
options: Joshua ignored worship to focus on rebuilding
Joshua built an altar and offered sacrifices as commanded by Moses
Joshua celebrated with feasting but no sacrifices
Joshua appointed new kings without worship
questions.correctAnswer: Joshua built an altar and offered sacrifices as commanded by Moses
questions.explanation: Joshua built an altar of whole stones and offered burnt and peace offerings according to Moses' command, demonstrating obedience and worship after victory (Joshua 8:30-31).

hard.title: Joshua Chapter 8 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Joshua Chapter 8.

questions.question: How many men, women, and children fell in the battle of Ai according to Joshua 8:25?
options: Ten thousand
Twelve thousand
Fifteen thousand
Eight thousand
questions.correctAnswer: Twelve thousand
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:25 states that all who fell that day were twelve thousand, both men and women.

questions.question: What did Joshua do with his hand while stretching out the spear during the conquest of Ai?
options: He withdrew it quickly
He drew it back slowly
He did not draw it back
He dropped it suddenly
questions.correctAnswer: He did not draw it back
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:26 explains that Joshua did not draw back his hand with which he stretched out the spear until all inhabitants were destroyed.

questions.question: What did Israel take as spoil from Ai?
options: Only the gold and silver
Only the cattle and spoil
Only the weapons
Everything including cattle and spoil
questions.correctAnswer: Only the cattle and spoil
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:27 states that only the cattle and spoil of Ai were taken for a prey according to the LORD's command.

questions.question: What did Joshua do to the city of Ai after its conquest?
options: Built a fortress
Burnt it down
Made it a royal city
Left it intact
questions.correctAnswer: Burnt it down
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:28 records that Joshua burnt Ai and made it a heap, a desolation unto this day.

questions.question: What was done to the king of Ai after he was captured?
options: He was set free
He was hanged on a tree until eventide
He was imprisoned for life
He was taken to Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: He was hanged on a tree until eventide
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:29 says the king of Ai was hanged on a tree until eventide, then his body was taken down and cast at the city gate.

questions.question: Where did Joshua build an altar unto the LORD after the conquest of Ai?
options: Mount Sinai
Mount Ebal
Mount Gerizim
Mount Zion
questions.correctAnswer: Mount Ebal
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:30 states that Joshua built an altar unto the LORD God of Israel on Mount Ebal.

questions.question: What was unique about the stones used for the altar Joshua built on Mount Ebal?
options: They were painted
No iron tool was used to shape them
They were gold-plated
They were imported from Jericho
questions.correctAnswer: No iron tool was used to shape them
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:31 records the altar was made of whole stones over which no man lifted up any iron, following Moses' command.

questions.question: What did Joshua write upon the stones on the altar?
options: The Ten Commandments only
A copy of the law of Moses
A song of praise
A list of kings defeated
questions.correctAnswer: A copy of the law of Moses
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:32 explains Joshua wrote a copy of the law of Moses upon the stones in the presence of Israel.

questions.question: Where did the people of Israel stand when Joshua read the law aloud?
options: Only on Mount Gerizim
Only on Mount Ebal
Half on Mount Gerizim and half on Mount Ebal
All on the plains of Jericho
questions.correctAnswer: Half on Mount Gerizim and half on Mount Ebal
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:33 states that half stood on Mount Gerizim and half on Mount Ebal as Moses commanded.

questions.question: What did Joshua read to all the congregation of Israel according to Joshua 8:34-35?
options: Only the blessings of the law
Only the curses of the law
All the words of the law, blessings and cursings
Only the Ten Commandments
questions.correctAnswer: All the words of the law, blessings and cursings
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:34-35 says Joshua read all words of the law including blessings and cursings before all Israel.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua allowed some inhabitants of Ai to escape after the battle.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: According to Joshua 8:22, none of the inhabitants of Ai remained or escaped after the battle.

questions.question: True or False: The altar built by Joshua on Mount Ebal was a fulfillment of Moses' command in the law.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:31-33 shows Joshua built the altar and performed the offerings exactly as Moses commanded in the law.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage does the reading of blessings and cursings in Joshua 8:34 echo?
options: Deuteronomy 27
Genesis 12
Exodus 20
Leviticus 16
questions.correctAnswer: Deuteronomy 27
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:34 echoes Deuteronomy 27 where blessings and cursings were proclaimed on Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal, fulfilling Moses' command.

questions.question: What is the significance of the term 'heap' used in Joshua 8:28 regarding Ai?
options: It signifies a permanent ruin
It means a pile of treasure
It denotes a newly built city
It refers to an altar
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies a permanent ruin
questions.explanation: 'Heap' in Joshua 8:28 means a ruin or desolation, indicating Ai was left destroyed permanently as a warning.

questions.question: The hanging of the king of Ai on a tree in Joshua 8:29 can be seen as a foreshadowing of which New Testament event?
options: Jesus' crucifixion
Paul's missionary journeys
Pentecost
The resurrection of Lazarus
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus' crucifixion
questions.explanation: The hanging of the king on a tree in Joshua 8:29 foreshadows Jesus' crucifixion on a tree as referenced in Acts 5:30 and Galatians 3:13.

theological.title: Joshua Chapter 8 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Joshua Chapter 8 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily demonstrated by the LORD's command to Joshua to fear not and not be dismayed in his battle against Ai?
options: God's omnipotence
God's mercy
God's patience
God's justice
questions.correctAnswer: God's omnipotence
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:1 shows God's omnipotence as He assures Joshua of victory by giving the king of Ai and his city into his hand, indicating divine power over enemies.

questions.question: According to Joshua 8, what was the purpose of the ambush set behind the city of Ai?
options: To protect the Israelites from surprise attack
To seize the city once the enemy was drawn out
To block the escape routes for the cattle
To negotiate peace with the king of Ai
questions.correctAnswer: To seize the city once the enemy was drawn out
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:7 explains that the ambush was to rise up and seize the city after drawing out the enemy, demonstrating a tactical military plan under divine guidance.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God's covenant faithfulness can be drawn from Joshua's adherence to God's command to take only the spoil and cattle for themselves?
options: God's commands are optional based on circumstances
God's covenant includes blessings contingent on obedience
God rewards disobedience with material gain
God is indifferent to Israel's conduct
questions.correctAnswer: God's covenant includes blessings contingent on obedience
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:2 and 8:27 show that Israel obeyed God's command to take only spoil and cattle, reflecting covenant faithfulness where blessings and conduct are linked.

questions.question: How does the tactic of feigning flight in verses 5-6 teach about the role of human agency in divine victory?
options: Victory comes solely by human wisdom
God acts without any human involvement
Human obedience and strategy cooperate with God's plan
Deception is condemned by God
questions.correctAnswer: Human obedience and strategy cooperate with God's plan
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:5-6 reveals that Joshua and Israel used a human tactical strategy of feigning flight, showing that divine victory often involves human agency cooperating with God's guidance.

questions.question: What is the theological significance of Joshua stretching out his spear toward Ai as commanded by the LORD?
options: It symbolizes human strength alone
It represents God's sovereign arm in battle
It is a mere military gesture with no meaning
It was a ritual to appease the gods of Ai
questions.correctAnswer: It represents God's sovereign arm in battle
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:18-19 shows that Joshua's act of stretching out his spear signifies the LORD's sovereign power delivering Ai into Israel's hands, an emblem of divine intervention.

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by the complete destruction of Ai's inhabitants except for the spoil and cattle taken by Israel?
options: Doctrine of universal salvation
Doctrine of divine judgment and holiness
Doctrine of human merit
Doctrine of predestination
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of divine judgment and holiness
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:24-27 records the utter destruction of Ai's people, showing God's judgment against sin and the call to holiness by separating the spoil as commanded, demonstrating divine holiness and justice.

questions.question: How does the hanging of the king of Ai on a tree until eventide relate to biblical typology and redemptive history?
options: It foreshadows Christ's crucifixion and curse bearing
It signifies a pagan ritual unrelated to Scripture
It demonstrates the king's innocence
It symbolizes Israel's defeat
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows Christ's crucifixion and curse bearing
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:29 typologically prefigures Christ who was hung on a tree bearing the curse for humanity (cf. Galatians 3:13), integrating this event into the broader redemptive narrative.

questions.question: What does Joshua's building of an altar and writing a copy of the law on stones on Mount Ebal teach about the role of the law in sanctification?
options: The law is obsolete after conquest
The law remains central for Israel's covenant obedience
The law is only ceremonial and symbolic
The law was replaced by military might
questions.correctAnswer: The law remains central for Israel's covenant obedience
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:30-32 shows that Joshua established the altar and inscribed the law as a covenantal foundation, highlighting the law's ongoing role in sanctification and obedience.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the violence in Joshua 8 contradicts the character of a loving God. What does Joshua 8:1-29 actually teach about God's justice and holiness in relation to sin?
options: God tolerates sin indefinitely
God's holiness demands judgment on sin, demonstrated in His justice
God is indifferent to human sin
God's love excludes any form of judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness demands judgment on sin, demonstrated in His justice
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:1-29 shows God's holy justice in commanding the destruction of sinful nations, affirming that His love coexists with righteous judgment against sin (cf. Romans 1:18).

questions.question: What combined teaching about divine guidance and human leadership can be drawn from Joshua 8:10 and 8:13 regarding Israel's approach to Ai?
options: Human leaders act independently of God
Divine guidance involves human leaders actively organizing and positioning the people
Leadership is unnecessary with divine intervention
Israel's leaders acted without faith
questions.correctAnswer: Divine guidance involves human leaders actively organizing and positioning the people
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:10 and 8:13 demonstrate Joshua's active leadership in numbering and positioning troops under God's command, showing cooperation between divine guidance and human responsibility.

questions.question: How does Joshua 8:34-35 emphasize the importance of the public reading of the law in Israel's covenant life?
options: It was a private act for priests only
It ensured communal knowledge and obedience among all people, including women and strangers
It was optional and rarely done
It replaced sacrifices entirely
questions.correctAnswer: It ensured communal knowledge and obedience among all people, including women and strangers
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:34-35 shows Joshua reading the law publicly to all Israel, including women and strangers, emphasizing the law's central role in covenant community and obedience.

questions.question: What theological insight does the valley location between Israel and Ai (Joshua 8:11) provide about spiritual warfare and God's provision?
options: Physical geography has no spiritual significance
God places His people in challenging situations to display His power
The valley represents defeat and abandonment
Israel fought without God’s presence
questions.correctAnswer: God places His people in challenging situations to display His power
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:11 mentions a valley separating Israel and Ai, symbolizing trials where God’s power is revealed through victory despite obstacles, a theme consistent with spiritual warfare (cf. Ephesians 6).

questions.question: What does the complete destruction of Ai's inhabitants and the burning of the city (Joshua 8:28) teach about God's requirement for holiness in His people’s conquest?
options: God allows Israel to keep idols
God requires thorough removal of sin and idolatry for covenant faithfulness
God condones partial obedience
God’s presence is unrelated to Israel's obedience
questions.correctAnswer: God requires thorough removal of sin and idolatry for covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:28 records the burning of Ai as a heap of desolation, symbolizing the necessity of holiness and complete removal of sin for Israel to remain faithful to God's covenant.

questions.question: How does Joshua 8:33 illustrate the inclusivity of the covenant community in Israel’s worship and law observance?
options: Only native-born men participated
Both strangers and born Israelites stood before the ark and heard the law
Women were excluded from the assembly
Only priests and Levites were present
questions.correctAnswer: Both strangers and born Israelites stood before the ark and heard the law
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:33 specifies that all Israel, including strangers and natives, stood before the ark, showing the covenant community included all who lived among Israel under God's law.

questions.question: What combined lesson about God's sovereignty and human responsibility is conveyed in Joshua 8:15-17 and Joshua 8:21-22 regarding the ambush strategy?
options: Victory was due only to human military skill
God sovereignly delivered the city despite human tactical action
The ambush was unnecessary for victory
Israel won by chance without God's help
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly delivered the city despite human tactical action
questions.explanation: Joshua 8:15-17 and 8:21-22 show Israel's tactical retreat and ambush, but the victory is attributed to the LORD's deliverance, combining divine sovereignty with human obedience.
